content.text: Based on my analysis of the diff and available knowledge of the Clerk ecosystem, I have a critical finding to report.

findings.explanation: The added dependency `@clerk/react` is not the official Clerk React SDK. Clerk's official, documented React SDK is published on npm as `@clerk/clerk-react` (see clerk.com docs). No package named `@clerk/react` is documented by Clerk or referenced in their official quickstarts. Because npm scopes (`@clerk/*`) are owned by the `clerk` organization, an unofficial `@clerk/react` published under this scope would either be (a) an unpublished/reserved namespace collision, (b) an internal/experimental package not meant for production consumption, or (c) most concerningly, evidence of a scope takeover / malicious publish. This is an authentication library — its code runs in every page load and handles session tokens, cookies, and identity — so a malicious or hijacked version could steal credentials, exfiltrate session cookies (its transitive dep pulls in `js-cookie`), inject arbitrary JS, or backdoor the auth flow. The lock file also pins `@clerk/shared@4.25.5` which does not correspond to Clerk's currently-published shared package version line (Clerk's `@clerk/shared` has been in the 2.x/3.x range historically). Even in the best case (an unofficial fork), taking on an auth library that isn't the vendor's blessed SDK for a production app is a serious supply-chain risk. Because `postinstall` scripts in any of the transitive packages would run on `npm install`, the risk isn't limited to runtime — it applies at CI/dev install time as well.
findings.fix: Do NOT install this dependency until verified. (1) Confirm the correct package name with Clerk's official docs — for React SPAs the intended package is almost certainly `@clerk/clerk-react`. Replace `"@clerk/react": "^6.12.5"` with `"@clerk/clerk-react": "^<current-version>"`. (2) If `@clerk/react` really is intentional, verify the publisher on npm (`npm view @clerk/react maintainers publisher`) matches the official Clerk org (`clerk` / `clerkinc`), inspect the tarball for unexpected postinstall scripts, and pin an exact version + integrity hash after review. (3) Add a lockfile-lint / socket.dev / npm audit signatures step to CI to catch scope-drift on future auth-critical deps.
